title: Improving Reset-Security Query Complexity
summary: One term in the reset-security reduction has quadratic dependence on p; whether the Barak–Mahmoody technique can make that dependence linear remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the reset-security reduction, the query complexity contains a term $8qp^2/\varepsilon$. Can the technique of Barak and Mahmoody be adapted to prove a corresponding query-complexity term of $O(qp)/\varepsilon$?

scope.domain: Query-complexity analysis of reset-security reductions for block-cipher security.
parameters: q: multiplicative parameter in both query-complexity terms
p: parameter with quadratic dependence in the current term and linear dependence in the conjectured term
ε: inverse factor in both query-complexity terms
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the Barak–Mahmoody technique can be adapted to prove the O(qp)/ε query-complexity term.

citations.label: Naor-Reingold Goes Public: The Complexity of Known-Key Security

progress.summary: The source states its belief that the Barak–Mahmoody technique can improve the term, but leaves this avenue unexplored because another proof approach was easier to adapt.
citation_labels: Pratik Soni et al., Naor-Reingold Goes Public: The Complexity of Known-Key Security
